venue_evaluation.night_market_hollow_oak: Out: peanuts are the house signature (peanut butter, satay sauce, peanut slaw). This is Cyrus's crossed-out stall.
venue_evaluation.campus_bun_stop: Safe but 2 stars: $, peanut-free, vegan black bean patty, but butter-toasted brioche, cheese on burgers and garlic-butter fries hit Roxy's dairy intolerance. Also it is at the north gate, not by the fountain.
venue_evaluation.night_market_amber_lamp: 3 stars: $, peanut-free kitchen checked thoroughly, black bean and mushroom meatless burgers, oil not butter, no cheese.
venue_evaluation.night_market_velvet_tent: Out: board is all meat, so nothing for Mina. Otherwise peanut-free, dairy-free and $.
venue_evaluation.night_market_midnight_orchard: 2 stars: peanut-free, dairy-free, meatless options, but $$ (one tier over) and reviews say it runs a couple of dollars more.
venue_evaluation.night_market_crooked_pine: Out: $$$ is two tiers over Maya's budget ('fancy prices and i'm turning around at the gate').

notes: Fair puzzle. Each decoy fails exactly one thing: Hollow Oak (peanut), Velvet Tent (no meatless option), Bun Stop (dairy), Midnight Orchard (one tier over), Crooked Pine (two tiers over).
Cyrus's peanut allergy is phrased indirectly ('Satay and I have history'); Liam's follow-up line makes it clear, so it is findable but needs one inference step.

Mina's diet is stated as 'zero meat', which reads as vegetarian. Several reviews talk about plant-based/vegan options, so a player might wonder whether she is vegan. Amber Lamp works either way (the mushroom stack is fully plant-based and there is no dairy), so it does not change the answer.

Small oddity: Liam says Mina had only fries at campus burger night because nothing worked for her, but the Bun Stop review says the vegan black bean patty has been on the campus board since 'the campus days'. That may be a deliberate trap pointing away from Bun Stop, or a small continuity slip; it does not affect the answer since Bun Stop already loses a star for dairy.
Roxy's dairy intolerance is a clear signal ('hold the cheese, no creamy sauce, no shake. my stomach makes the rules') and reads as an intolerance, not an allergy.
